status_summary: No enacted law or bill restricting FHA single-family insurance to first-time homebuyers, moving HECM to its own fund, revising single-family loan limit determinations or adding shorter-term product flexibility was found. The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, Public Law 119-101, became law without signature on 2026-07-11 after presentment on 2026-06-29; per the Congressional Research Service it touches FHA through Mutual Mortgage Insurance Fund capital reporting, counseling, appraisals, a small-dollar mortgage pilot and multifamily loan limits, and does not address the listed single-family items.
title: Legislate FHA changes: first-time buyer limit, HECM fund, loan limits, shorter terms
uncertainties: In review the CRS report on Public Law 119-101 was read in full across two passes: it confirms the law number, enactment on 2026-07-11 without the President's signature after presentment on 2026-06-29, origin in H.R. 6644, and finds no provisions on HECM, single-family FHA loan limits, first-time homebuyers, shorter-term mortgages or AFFH; section 211 concerns multifamily loan limits and section 303 Title I loan limits. Because the law does not touch the listed items it is not treated as a parallel step. Bills outside that law were searched once by the researcher and none was found; congress.gov pages could not be opened. The draft's title and proposal described ending the first-time limit; the text instead favors restricting FHA single-family insurance to first-time homebuyers, and the record was corrected. The premium element is tracked in c15-12. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register searches, agenda and proposed-rule listings, a congress.gov and govinfo.gov bill search, the HUD newsroom and a news search found no law, bill or rule restricting FHA insurance to first-time buyers, moving the reverse mortgage program to its own fund, revising single-family loan limit determinations or allowing shorter terms. On the closing clause only, HUD's interim final rule of 2025-03-03 revised the affirmatively furthering fair housing certification for grantees and public housing agencies, not FHA single-family programs, and HUD's proposed rule of 2025-06-03 would rescind the affirmative fair housing marketing regulations that apply to FHA insurance participants, including some single-family applicants; no final rescission was found. Not_started was kept because the recommendation is a statutory revision whose four main items are untouched, the affirmative-obligation clause is tracked in c15-01, and the marketing rescission is a proposal; proposed 5 is the other defensible call if the marketing rescission is counted as a partial step on the closing clause. HUD's October 2025 request for information on the HECM program seeks comment on improvements and mentions no separate insurance fund.
